title: Ingress-shim annotations and HTTP-01 solvers cross the Ingress v1 migration

detection.reason: names the Ingresses that carry a cert-manager shim annotation; whether THIS ingress controller has a known v1 issue is what the vendor's compatibility page answers, and that is not on the cluster

quote: If you are currently using HTTP-01 challenges or the Ingress shim annotations, please read the Ingress class compatibility notes to see if your Ingress controller has any known issues with the migration to Ingress v1.
remediation: Read the vendor's Ingress class compatibility notes for your ingress controller before upgrading: from 1.5 both the ingress-shim (Ingresses annotated `cert-manager.io/…`) and the HTTP-01 solver Ingresses are written as networking.k8s.io/v1. Afterwards re-check that shim-managed Ingresses and HTTP-01 challenges still get certificates issued.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ingress -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(any((.metadata.annotations // {}) | keys[]; test("^cert-manager\\.io/"))) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) class=\(.spec.ingressClassName // "-")"'  # each row is an Ingress whose certificate depends on the shim

title: HTTP-01 solver Ingresses cross the Ingress v1 migration

detection.reason: names the issuers whose ACME solvers create Ingresses; whether THIS ingress controller has a known v1 issue is what the vendor's compatibility page answers, and that is not on the cluster

quote: If you are currently using HTTP-01 challenges or the Ingress shim annotations, please read the Ingress class compatibility notes to see if your Ingress controller has any known issues with the migration to Ingress v1.
remediation: Read the vendor's Ingress class compatibility notes for your ingress controller before upgrading: from 1.5 both the ingress-shim (Ingresses annotated `cert-manager.io/…`) and the HTTP-01 solver Ingresses are written as networking.k8s.io/v1. Afterwards re-check that shim-managed Ingresses and HTTP-01 challenges still get certificates issued.
verifyCommand: kubectl get issuers,clusterissuers -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | . as $i | .spec.acme.solvers[]? | select(.http01.ingress) | "\($i.kind)/\($i.metadata.namespace // "cluster")/\($i.metadata.name) class=\(.http01.ingress.class // .http01.ingress.ingressClassName // "-")"'  # each row creates solver Ingresses as networking.k8s.io/v1 from 1.5

title: Legacy API versions v1alpha2/v1alpha3/v1beta1 are deprecated — stop serving at 1.6, gone from the CRDs at 1.7

detection.reason: every cert-manager 1.3-1.6 CRD declares v1alpha2/v1alpha3/v1beta1, so the version LIST cannot tell a migrated cluster from one that is not; `status.storedVersions`, which can, is not projected

quote: Additionally, the cert-manager API versions `v1alpha2`, `v1alpha3` and `v1beta1` are now deprecated, and will be removed in cert-manager 1.7. Please change all your YAML manifests that use a deprecated API version to use `cert-manager.io/v1` instead, and re-apply them.
remediation: Only a cluster that ran cert-manager before v1.0 can still have objects stored at a legacy version — the command below settles it. Convert every manifest to `cert-manager.io/v1` (`cmctl convert`), and on 1.6, BEFORE upgrading to 1.7, run `cmctl upgrade migrate-api-version` (cmctl 1.7+): it rewrites the objects at v1 and sets each CRD's `status.storedVersions` to `[v1]`. Re-applying manifests alone does not update storedVersions.
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.group | test("cert-manager\\.io$")) as $c | $c.status.storedVersions[] | select(. != "v1") | "\($c.metadata.name) still stores \(.)"'  # each row is a CRD still storing a legacy version (clusters that predate v1.0); NO rows = only your manifests need converting
